title: Interactive lock reap timeout
author: author-a
description: Day 1 records a specific numeric timeout for a locking/claim mechanism: an INTERACTIVE claim (a live human session, confirmed by a live PID) gets a much longer hard reap timeout than an ordinary automated claim. The exact minute count is an arbitrary tuning choice with no natural default, so a memory-less model cannot guess it from the day-N prompt or general systems-design knowledge — a lock timeout could plausibly be anywhere from minutes to days.
day1_prompt: Day 1: we are tuning our region-lock reaper. Decide and record: an ordinary automated claim gets a hard reap timeout of 60 minutes, but an INTERACTIVE claim (a live human session, confirmed by a live PID on the same host) gets a much longer hard reap timeout of 720 minutes before the reaper is allowed to remove it.
memory_sentence: This project's lock reaper gives an INTERACTIVE claim (confirmed live PID) a hard reap timeout of 720 minutes, versus 60 minutes for an ordinary automated claim.
canon_heading: Interactive lock hard reap timeout is 720 minutes
day_n_prompt: Day 9: a developer asks how long an INTERACTIVE claim (one held by a live human session) can survive before our lock reaper is allowed to remove it. Answer with only the number of minutes.
